### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**41** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30b0987cd5187535cf09c32b18a83e73e9ee45a5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c58829ca001e72957386f8c6ce0a4e9e4bc1cbe8` — the merge of head `a6052bd68e580c46ab7cd0a7687bc3650a24ce23` into base `30b0987cd5187535cf09c32b18a83e73e9ee45a5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c58829ca001e72957386f8c6ce0a4e9e4bc1cbe8 && git checkout c58829ca001e72957386f8c6ce0a4e9e4bc1cbe8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 30b0987cd5187535cf09c32b18a83e73e9ee45a5 a6052bd68e580c46ab7cd0a7687bc3650a24ce23 && git checkout -B drift-repro 30b0987cd5187535cf09c32b18a83e73e9ee45a5 && git merge --no-ff a6052bd68e580c46ab7cd0a7687bc3650a24ce23

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30b0987cd5187535cf09c32b18a83e73e9ee45a5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): CHANGES** at head `c2895183af` (Fixes #35113 ask kinds on the dataset cards; Fixes #35098 folded, the step-2 approver prose). Both cards are delivered and the scope reading holds. One rule this round states is not held by the code, and one changeset sentence is false for this PR. Both are text-or-one-line fixes.

**Gates on this head:** `l1-face --pr 36065`: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` success; 32 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed, 4 pending (Test Core 1-4/10) at read time. One flag, `Fixes #35098`, is intended: the fold is recorded on #35098 (7061956379). Dogfood battery not owed. Local at this head: `vitest run test/dataset-cards.test.ts test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`, 2 files passed.

**C1. `owner_latest` is said to be held to "a `groupBy` on the person field", but the loader accepts any `groupBy`.**
- `questionKindProblem` (`src/ask-kinds.ts`) returns no problem for `owner_latest` whenever `t.groupBy !== undefined`. It never looks at which field is grouped.
- My probe (temporary test, reverted): set `orders_by_status` (`groupBy: "status"`) to `askKind: "owner_latest"` on `order_to_cash`. The card **loads**, with no refusal at any `askKind` path.
- Four places say otherwise: the README "Held to" cell ("a `groupBy` on the person field"), the loader message ("its truth groups by the person field it names"), the `schema.ts` comment block, and the PR body ("`owner_latest` a `groupBy` on the person field"). The message ships in `dist`.
- So `owner_latest` is not told apart from `group_sum` by anything the loader checks, while the docs say it is.
- **Fix, either way:** (a) hold it. Refuse `owner_latest` unless the `groupBy` path ends on a field whose seed values are person ids (the card's people, e.g. `approver`, `owner`, `claimant`), and add the refusal case `owner_latest` on `orders_by_status`. Or (b) say what is held. Reword the four places to "a `groupBy` (the person field the question names; the loader checks that it groups, not which field)". (b) is enough for this card.

**C2. The 35113 changeset says "The card files change only by the added `askKind` keys". In this PR, `travel_expense.json` also changes its detailed prompt (the #35098 commit).**
- Both changesets ship in the same release notes, so the sentence is false there.
- **Fix:** "`order_to_cash` changes only by the added `askKind` keys, `travel_expense` also by the #35098 prompt line, so both cards' sha256 move …", or drop "only".

**What I checked (holds):**
- **The Scope reading (a4-B's ask) is sound.** "Questions added until every kind is asked at least twice" is met with zero additions, counted either way:
  - Per turn: the README table. My count from the cards matches it.
  - Per distinct question (stricter): `top_n` 2 (top_accounts_billed, top_claimants), `time_range` 2 (collected_by_team_last_30_days as sales_manager, claimed_last_month), `unanswerable` 2, `forbidden` 3 (collected_by_team_last_30_days as sales_rep, department_budgets as employee, trips_by_status as finance_officer). Every other kind is at 3 or more.
  - `forbidden` is asked as member personas (sales_rep, employee), as the Scope asks. Every question has `zh` and `en`. No question is copied: none is added.
- **Done-when.** The table has no kind at zero. "One ask round reports every kind" is shown on the offline `runHalf` round. The kind is stamped from the card, not from the driver, so the tally does not depend on the live model. The first live daily round will show the row. I accept the offline evidence, with that note.
- **The per-turn `forbidden` rule** matches the runner. `askTurns` and `runHalf` both ask a persona-scoped question once per persona, and both read `personaTruths[q.id][persona]`.
- **Tally and render.** A kind's pass is the Run-问数 pass (`answerPassed`) or the dataset grade. Not-measured asks are out of the total. An unasked kind shows `0 asked`. `summary` counts a run without kinds apart (`missingText`).
- **#35098.** Finance is `e13` + `e14`, and `dep_fin.manager` is `e14`. All 90 seeded step-2 rows name `e13`, and `manager_approves_step_one` expects `approver: e13`. The prose fix (en + zh) removes the ambiguity, and truth, seed and operation are unchanged. Its changeset sentences hold.
- **Changesets.** Both are `@objectstack/scenarios: patch` on a public package. 35113: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right (new optional key and new exports); that is the seat's contract read. Sentence by sentence, everything holds except C2.
- **Provenance.** The `cardSha256` bump without a re-authored build follows #35764. The PR body says the verified build was authored on the old prose.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
- N1. The `schema.ts` comment says `checkAskKinds` is "in `loader.ts`". It lives in `ask-kinds.ts` and is called from the loader.
- N2. A kind cell with not-measured asks reads `forbidden 1/1 · 1 not measured · unanswerable …`. The same ` · ` separates kinds and the suffix. It is readable, and only noted.

**Next:** after the fix round, I delta-read C1 and C2 only. Then the seat does the Clause-② contract read and lands.

The one flag, `Fixes #35098`, is the intended fold. Dogfood battery not owed. Local at this head: `vitest run test/dataset-cards.test.ts`, 49 passed (the two open cards load).

**C1 (closed, held rather than reworded).**
- `groupsByPerson(card, object, groupBy)` walks every hop but the last through the card's declared `expect.lookups`. It answers yes only when the last hop is a declared lookup to an object a persona `record` names, or a declared `run.userHandleFields` entry. A hop no lookup declares answers no.
- `owner_latest` now needs `groupBy !== undefined && groupsByPerson(...)`. My earlier probe case, `orders_by_status` (`groupBy: status`) as `owner_latest`, is now a pinned refusal, and so is `booked_by_category`. `overdue_by_owner` (`account.owner`) is the load case.
- The three `owner_latest` questions on the cards (`so_0120_waiting_on`, `harbor_recent_followups`, `ec_0093_waiting_on`) still load, as the 49 green show.
- The README "Held to" cell, the loader message, the `schema.ts` comment, the changeset and the PR body now all say the same rule.

**C2 (closed).** The changeset now says "`order_to_cash` changes only by the added `askKind` keys, and `travel_expense` also by the step-2 approver line of its build prompt (the changeset beside this one), so both cards' sha256 move". That is true of the diff.

**N1 (fixed).** The `schema.ts` comment now says "`checkAskKinds` in `ask-kinds.ts`, called from `loader.ts`".

**S1, owed before landing (declaration, one line):** `groupsByPerson` is `export`ed from `src/ask-kinds.ts`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports `*` from it. So it is a new export at the package root. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line in the PR body and in the 35113 changeset lists the new exports, and it does not name this one. Either drop the `export` (only `questionKindProblem` calls it, and no test imports it), or add `groupsByPerson` to both lists. This folds into the seat's Clause-② contract read. No L1 re-read is needed for a list edit or a dropped keyword.

**Landing:** the seat's Clause-② contract read (with S1), then the seat lands. `Fixes #35098` is the intended fold (7061956379).

### ① Derived judgments

**Q1. Is the widening declaration complete, exact and purely additive?** No. There is one blocking finding and one should-fix.

- **F1 (must-fix): an undeclared narrowing at the card loader.** `checkAskKinds` (`src/ask-kinds.ts`) sets `required = card.run.datasetQuestions !== undefined`. On such a card it refuses every question and every dataset question that has no `askKind`, and `checkCard` in `loader.ts` calls it for every card. `run.datasetQuestions` has already shipped: the 18.6.0 changelog entry e4a16d0 added it. So `loadScenarios` / `loadScenarioFile` now refuse a card they loaded before: any card with dataset questions written against the released schema, including a `--cards DIR` overlay. The PR's own refusal cases prove it. `a question with no kind on a card that asks dataset questions` and `a dataset question with no kind` both expect `card` to be undefined, and the two open cards load only because this diff adds the key to them. The package has already declared this same shape as a narrowing: c0f88b9 (new optional keys, and the loader refusing a card it loaded before without them) carried `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, a **BREAKING** banner and an ADR-0087 disposition marker. Here the `(widening)` arm alone sends the PR to the declaration face and a lower landing tier than it owes. Pick one fix:
  - **(a), recommended, keeps the PR additive:** require the kinds only on a card that names at least one kind. Every question and dataset question then names one, all or none. No released card carries `askKind`, so no card that loaded before is refused. The open-library requirement stays pinned by `dataset-cards.test.ts`'s `every question and dataset question names its kind`. Re-aim the two missing-kind refusal cases at a card that names one kind but not all of them. Align these texts with the new rule: the loader message, the `DatasetQuestionSchema.askKind` TSDoc (it says "every dataset question names one"), README row 4 and the "Ask kinds" opening sentence, the package README bullet, and the changeset sentence "A card that asks dataset questions names the kind of every question it asks". The `(widening)` arm then stands, once S1 is fixed.
  - **(b) declare it:** use the `(narrowing)` arm in the PR body and the changeset (at most one arm, so the widening items move into the prose after it), add a **BREAKING** banner with the FROM → TO line (add `askKind` to every question and dataset question of a card that has `run.datasetQuestions`), and add an ADR-0087 disposition marker, as c0f88b9 did. This moves the PR to the narrowing face. It then owes a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record, and the declared narrowing lands the Tier H way. This record does not cover that.
- **S1 (should-fix; the L1 finding, confirmed):** `groupsByPerson` is a new root export. It is `export`ed from `src/ask-kinds.ts`, which `src/index.ts` re-exports with `export *`, and no declaration names it. Across all five entries, the export-set diff between merge-base and head shows nothing removed. Root: 96 → 105 names, the nine added being `ASK_KINDS`, `AskKind`, `AskKindSchema`, `AskTurn`, `askKindCounts`, `askTurns`, `checkAskKinds`, `questionTurnKind` and the undeclared `groupsByPerson`. `./runner`: 329 → 332, adding `KindTally`, `kindCell` and `kindTally`, all declared. `./score`, `./score/full` and `./export` are unchanged. So `groupsByPerson` is the only undeclared addition. Either drop `export` (only `questionKindProblem` calls it, and no test imports it), or name it in all three places: the PR-body `Clause-②` line, the changeset's `Clause-②` line, and the changeset's "New exports:" sentence.
- Every other item holds. The optional key `askKind` on `QuestionSchema` and `DatasetQuestionSchema` is declared. The optional fields `QuestionResult.askKind`, `DatasetQuestionResult.askKind` and `HalfScores.kinds` are declared. The new `Run · kinds` / `Iterate · Run · kinds` rows (in `renderScorecard` and `summary`) appear only when a turn carries a kind. No released card or record carries one, so the output of every existing export is unchanged for existing input.

**Q3. Is `askKind` validated, documented and backward compatible?** It is validated and documented. It is backward compatible except for F1.
- Validated: the key is a closed `z.enum(ASK_KINDS)` on two strict objects (the pinned `a kind outside the closed set` case). The loader checks each declared kind against its truth or route. There are 18 pinned refusal cases, each located at its `askKind` path. Two load cases cover a person reached across a lookup (`owner_latest`) and a declared `forbidden`.
- Documented: the `docs/qa/scenarios/README.md` "Ask kinds" table (kind, what it asks, what it is held to), the package README bullet, and the TSDoc on both keys and on the result fields.
- Backward compatible: a card without dataset questions loads unchanged (pinned). An older run record shows no row: `kindTally` returns undefined when no ask carries a kind, and `summary` counts such a run apart instead of as 0 asked. A card with dataset questions is refused: F1.

**Q4. Is the provenance hash update legitimate under the #35764 precedent?** Yes, with one note.
- `cardSha256` `29162eef…` equals the sha256 of the head card, and `abe91b8f…` is the merge-base card. The build file is byte-unchanged (`5fe6f452…` at both trees), and `order_to_cash` has no verified build, so it owes no provenance.
- The card diff touches only `prompt.detailed` and the `askKind` lines. `expect`, `seed` and `personas` are byte-unchanged, so the recorded `verified` 135/135 and 757/757 hold against the new card by construction.
- **N1:** #35764 justified its in-PR update by "the build half renders `prompt.*` and the `expect` rows, never `run.questions`". This diff also moves `prompt.detailed`, which the build half does render, so that reason does not carry over word for word. What holds it here is the comment 7061940514 measurement: the unchanged build's flow already routes step 2 to e13, 6/6 on published 18.6.0. Only the PR body says the build was authored from the pre-#35098 prompt. The provenance file says nothing about it. That is acceptable, and it is a nit.

**Q5. Does the #35098 prose fix match the card's own seed (e13)?** Yes.
- At the head, the Finance department (`dep_fin`) has two employees, e13 and e14, and its `manager` is e14. So "a Finance officer (Finance staff other than the finance manager)" picks e13 alone, and so does 一名财务专员(财务经理以外的财务人员).
- All 90 seeded `approval_step` rows with `step: 2` name e13. The `finance_officer` persona is "Finance officer, organization-wide — e13".
- `manager_approves_step_one` still expects the step-2 row `approver: e13, decision: pending`.
- The parenthetical "a manager's own claim goes to the finance manager" stays consistent: e14 approves 29 step-1 rows.

**Q6. Do the tests pin the floor of at least two asks per kind?** Yes. `across the two cards no kind is asked fewer than twice` fails on any kind whose two-card total is below 2. That is #35113's "at least twice across the dataset cards", counted per turn as the README states. `each card asks each kind as many times as the README table states` pins the exact table. Counted per distinct question, every kind also reaches 2.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/scenarios` is right for both changesets. Under ruling A, the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone. The scenario card format is a devx instrument, not the metadata protocol: the package description says so, and `packages/spec` is untouched. So `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The package's own precedents match: e4a16d0 added `run.datasetQuestions` at `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `none` / `patch`, and 35132 likewise. Under F1 option (b), the level stays `patch`, and the BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition carry the narrowing. The 35098 changeset (`Clause-②: no`, `none`, `patch`) matches its prose-only card change, as #35764 did.

The README hunk teaches the platform's field-level-security masking (ADR-0106 D4/D8: a hidden field does not exist in a plain member's schema), and the `forbidden` kind grades leak readings. No permission, sharing or auth code changes. The PR touches no governed path, so the line gates no arm here.

  - The two NOT-MEASURED local gates (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) were left to CI, and no check on this head failed.
  - No live model round ran. The offline `runHalf` round stands in for it, and Done-when's live row is left to the first live round.

Findings: F1 (must-fix), S1 (should-fix), N1 (nit). FAIL on F1. After fix (a) and S1, a delta read on the new head closes this record. If fix (b) is chosen, a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record is owed on the new head instead.
